decision.reason: The independently recomputed fair A1-OSG baseline has zero off-chip psum spill under 240 KiB. LB-FUSE forms 1.413364871707x groups, incurs 1.151893823294x on-chip psum RMW bytes, and is 8.273802 percent slower overall despite the candidate-favorable D3 Acc16 choice.

numeric_audit.scope: local per-output-channel INT8 scheduling and width probe; not checkpoint numeric or accuracy admission

finding.p2_precision_wording: Do not describe the entire comparison as matched-Acc24: the fair A1 baseline is Acc24 throughout, while the selected D3 LB candidate receives trace-bounded Acc16 to fit full width. This favors LB-FUSE and therefore cannot overturn the kill, but it must be disclosed.

may_cite: Negative design-space ablation: on the complete sealed M705 S3x10 local-INT8 probe, fair A1-OSG was 1/0.923584454412 = 1.082738x faster than source-order LB-FUSE.
Mechanism diagnosis: source-order issue created 1.413364871707x destination groups and 1.151893823294x on-chip psum RMW bytes while both designs had zero off-chip psum spill.
Sequence robustness of the negative result: A1/LB was 0.926111, 0.923851, and 0.920822 on the three selected sequences.
Selected-trace width observation: D3 local-INT8 absolute-prefix bound was 7288, whereas D0 reached 62696; this is not a universal or accuracy proof.
must_not_claim: RTL, VCS, synthesis, PPA, or energy evidence
line buffer, polyphase mapping, or Acc16 as a new invention
population-wide generalization beyond the three selected sequences
